subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a general temp-artifact provenance and cleanup model, or should core only add runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal provenance seam for plugins/skills?
rationale: The issue is valid, but the durable storage owner, cleanup authority, and boundary between core safety checks and workflow-specific janitor behavior require maintainer product intent before implementation.

options.title: Core Guardrails Plus Minimal Seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full Core Provenance Registry
options.body: Build a core-owned artifact classification and cleanup policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader state and janitor responsibility in core.

options.title: Plugin Or Skill Workflow
options.body: Keep artifact provenance outside core except for concrete runtime-critical bug reports and publish the janitor/classification workflow through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Core Guardrails Plus Minimal Seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest available routing owner for the core-vs-ClawHub boundary decision from the related issue discussion and recent merge history.
